events.type: Industry read-across: memory maker (peer of largest customer) preliminary results
events.summary: Samsung Electronics' preliminary Q3 2026 results: operating profit about 107.40 trillion won (range 107.3-107.5tn) and sales about 195 trillion won (range 194-196tn). A year earlier (Q3 2025): operating profit 12.17tn, sales 86.06tn; previous quarter (Q2 2026): operating profit 89.49tn, sales 171.5tn [Samsung newsroom, 2026-10-08]. Our arithmetic: operating profit +782.5% year on year and +20.0% from Q2; sales +126.6% year on year and +13.7% from Q2. Consensus before the release: operating profit 105.41tn and sales 200.26tn won (Yonhap, as cited by TrendForce), or 106.94tn operating profit (Chosun Ilbo, as cited by TrendForce) [TrendForce, 2026-10-07]. So profit beat by about 1.9% (vs Yonhap) / 0.4% (vs Chosun) and sales missed by about 2.6% (our arithmetic). Korea Herald: first tech company to top 100 trillion won of quarterly profit; driven by 'booming demand for high-bandwidth memory used in AI computing and sharply higher prices for conventional memory chips'; analysts estimate the memory business made about 110tn won; 'tight HBM supply continues to support prices' into next year; Samsung is 'expanding HBM production lines in Pyeongtaek' and pursuing longer-term sites in Yongin and Gwangju; a stronger won reduced the won value of dollar chip sales and the mobile division lost about 1.5tn won [Korea Herald, 2026-10-08]. Samsung's preliminary release gives only two numbers; no division breakdown or spending plan (full results later in October, date not found). Market reaction: memory shares fell anyway. Samsung closed 262,000 won, -2.42% in Seoul on 10-08 (Yahoo Finance chart data; the Korea Herald reports a close of 263,500 won, -1.86%: the two sources disagree); SK hynix -2.44% in Seoul (1,681,000 won) and -4.35% on its US listing SKHY; Micron -4.79%; Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) -5.13% (Yahoo Finance chart data; our arithmetic). Korean markets did not trade Friday 10-09 (Hangul Day holiday; inference, high confidence: Yahoo's last Seoul bar is 10-08).
events.why_it_matters: FormFactor's thesis trigger 2 is 'memory makers cut spending'. Samsung's record memory profit, tight HBM supply and expanding HBM production lines point the other way: memory makers are earning more and adding HBM capacity, which is what drives probe-card orders (DRAM probe cards were 32.9% of FormFactor's Q2 revenue, and HBM made up about 75% of the year-on-year DRAM increase [FormFactor 10-Q, 2026-08-04]). Samsung itself is not a 10%-plus FormFactor customer (only SK hynix 24.3%, TSMC 11.0% were in Q2), so this is a read-across on the memory cycle, not a direct order signal. The fact that memory shares fell on record results shows investors are worried about how long the boom lasts, which moves FormFactor's share price even when the business news is good.

products.name: Probe cards for DRAM and high-bandwidth memory (HBM)
products.what_it_is: A custom test board covered in thousands of microscopic needles that touches every memory chip on a wafer at once to check it works before the wafer is cut up and the chips are stacked into HBM.
products.analogy: Like a custom-cut key made for one lock: every new chip design needs its own card, and the key wears out with use, so the chipmaker keeps ordering more.
products.buyers: Memory makers. SK hynix was 24.3% of FormFactor's Q2 2026 revenue; TSMC 11.0%; no other customer reached 10% [FormFactor 10-Q, 2026-08-04]. Whether Samsung or Micron buy FormFactor HBM cards in volume is not disclosed.
products.how_it_works: A machine called a prober presses the card onto the wafer; a tester sends signals through the needles into each chip and records which pass. HBM stacks several memory chips on top of each other, so each chip has to be checked before stacking (background explanation, not from a source today).
products.sales: HBM sales not disclosed separately. Proxy: DRAM probe-card revenue $85.0m in Q2 2026 (32.9% of total revenue), up 49.0% from $57.1m a year earlier; HBM accounted for about 75% of that year-on-year DRAM increase. First half 2026 DRAM revenue $167.9m (34.7% of revenue).
products.size_for_company: DRAM probe cards were 32.9% of Q2 revenue; at the Q2 rate that is about $340m a year (our arithmetic: $85.0m x 4), against total Q2 revenue of $258.2m. The largest market is still Foundry & Logic at $121.8m (47.2%).
products.competition: Not researched in this run. Other probe-card makers include Technoprobe (Italy) and Micronics Japan (background knowledge, not sourced today).
products.why_investors_care: HBM is FormFactor's fastest-growing product line and is tied directly to memory makers adding HBM capacity, which Samsung's record results and expanding Pyeongtaek HBM lines suggest is continuing [Korea Herald, 2026-10-08].
products.watch_next: DRAM revenue line and HBM commentary in Q3 results on 2026-10-28 and the next 10-Q; SK hynix Q3 results (reported for 2026-10-27, tier 3).
